reason: A quality adjective (denticulate lobules, denticulate scales), not a structure. The counted bearers are lobules and scales of an organ the clause does not name. 'lobule' and 'scale' alone were rejected as generic on 2026-11-13.

Narrower name: the scale-like segments of a divided or dissected floral disc (FLOPO_0986025). The nearest existing class is floral disc lobe. Where the segments are glandular, disc gland (FLOPO_0986045) is the alternative. Fleshy and oblong fit disc segments.

Narrower name. 'cone scale' and 'ovuliferous scale' are already synonyms of megasporophyll. 'Fertile' picks out the seed-bearing scales of a conifer cone, as against the sterile ones. Unlike the rejected 'fertile scale', the word 'cone' removes the Cyperaceae glume sense. Counts use pattern 03.

A fragment: 'ones' stands for a part named earlier (stamens, flowers). 'Fertile' (PATO_0000955) is already a context word for stamen, flower and so on, and 'fertile' alone was rejected as not a structure.

'apophysis' alone was rejected because it has two senses, moss capsule base or Pinus scale end. 'Fruit scale' (cone scale) fixes the Pinus sense: the exposed, thickened distal end of the ovuliferous scale. It is expressed as the apex region of megasporophyll. Do NOT map it to sporangium base (PO_0030040), whose synonym 'apophysis' is the moss sense. If more floras need it, a PO request for 'ovuliferous scale apophysis' could follow.
A generic 'segment' with no organ ('divided into 2-11 further segments'). It is the next order of division of a leaf, lobe or frond. 'segment' was rejected as generic on 2026-11-13.

Narrower name: a flat glandular area on a lamina or bract. 'gland' is already a synonym of PO_0005656. Where it sits near the petiole on the leaf it may be an extrafloral nectary (PO_0009057), but colour words like 'blue' do not confirm nectar secretion, so the general gland class is safer.
A colour quality taken from a phrase that counts other parts ('1-3 pairs of green spines', 'green longitudinal stripes'). It is not a structure.

target: plant cell (PO_0009002) part_of sporangium (PO_0025094), counted with pattern 03
reason: Narrower name: the indurated (thick-walled) cells of a fern sporangium annulus. Their number is a standard fern character. Annulus cells are a kind of plant cell, part of the sporangium. 'annulus' alone was rejected as generic, and PO's spore capsule annulus (PO_0025093) is the moss sense, so it must not be used.

target: plant organ apex (FLOPO_0985023) part_of labellum lobe (FLOPO_0986028) part_of hypochile (FLOPO_0986030)
reason: The apex region of a lobe of the orchid hypochile. All parts exist: hypochile, labellum lobe and the apex region. Acute and subacute are apex shapes.

An arrangement with a count ('cupules in clusters of 2 or 3'), not a structure. 'clustered' was rejected in the same way. Use the quality clustered or fascicled (FLOPO:0991098) with a count of the named part.
A position in a series. 'lateral' is a bearer_quality context word that already lists 'cyme', and 'cyme' is a synonym of PO_0030126. Length, width and count apply to the lateral cymes.

Narrower (collective) name: 'lateral venation' means the lateral, secondary veins of the blade. Do not use lateral leaf vein (PO_0006011), which PO defines as the grass-type second-order vein between primary veins. Inconspicuous and present apply to the veins.

A union of two different parts ('leaflets or lobes 3-11'): leaflet (PO_0020049) of a compound leaf or lobe of a simple one. The lobe has no organ. Like 'teeth or lobe' and 'lobes or teeth', it is not one structure.

A generic tooth of an unnamed organ (margin of a leaf, calyx or bract) plus the quality 'long'. Where the clause names the leaf, leaf lamina tooth (PO_0025518) with increased length applies. Without that it needs context.
A ratio fragment ('1/2 height of nutlet'): pattern 10 (ratio to another part), with nut fruit (PO_0030102, synonym nutlet) as the other part.
A position fragment of a count ('6-14 [veins or pinnae] on each side of costa'). The counted part is named earlier in the sentence. Costa is leaf midvein (PO_0020139) or costa (PO_0030072).
A quality (finely pilose) of domatia ('with pilosulous domatia'). The bearer is domatium (FLOPO_0986021).

The part of a rachis that extends beyond the last lateral member. It occurs on leaf rachises (paripinnate legumes: leaf rachis PO_0020055) and on grass inflorescence rachises beyond the last spikelet (inflorescence axis PO_0020122). 'rachis' alone was rejected as generic. Both senses use the apex region of the right rachis, but which rachis it is needs context.
Hairs on the rachis internodes of grass racemes (Andropogoneae), compared with spikelet length. Trichome as part of the inflorescence axis internode. The ratio to the spikelet is pattern 10.

Without family context it is not clear what structure this is: the central resin-secreting staminodial mass of Clusia flowers, the resin gland of Dalechampia, and so on. It could be a secretory tissue (PO_0005656) or a synandrium-like body (FLOPO_0986014).
A ratio fragment ('bracts 1/4-1/3 as long as seed scales'): pattern 10, with megasporophyll (PO_0009027, ovuliferous/seed scale) as the other part.

target: plant organ base (FLOPO_0985024) part_of leaf sheath (PO_0020104)
reason: The base region of the leaf sheath, persistent as remains, as in palms and grasses. A region of an existing class that the patterns can express.

reason: The apex region of the terminal lobe. 'terminal lobe' is an exact synonym of the positioned part terminal leaf lamina lobe. Where the flora describes an orchid lip, the lobe is a labellum lobe (FLOPO_0986028) instead.
Degree of branching ('lobes 1-3 times forked'): the quality branched/dichotomous with a count of orders, as 'times branched' was decided. It is not a structure.

A tuft of hairs is a hair distribution, not a part: the quality bearded (FLOPO:0991118) of the organ or region that bears it. This follows the rejection of 'tuft' and 'tufted'. Where a seed tuft is meant, coma (PO_0020061) applies.
The apex region of a tree fern trunk: tomentose, and surpassing the youngest fronds. Trunk and the apex region both exist.
In Carex, 'utricle' is the perigynium, and its stipe is the narrowed stalk at its base. 'stipe' already maps to stalk (C264). Length and short apply to the stalk.
A ratio fragment ('internodes 2-4 X as long as leaves'): pattern 10, with leaf (PO_0025034) as the other part.
A ratio fragment ('4-5 × as long as sepals'): pattern 10, with sepal (PO_0009031) as the other part, like 'times sepal' and 'x sepal length'.
